CI: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/52267#019c76d8-b9da-48ff-8834-2707ef78dc7e - 19.02.2026

test_pre_quantized_model

Summary:
The error:
                                 
  assert config.version == 2, f"Unexpected version: {config.version}"         
  AssertionError: Unexpected version: 1                                       
                                                                              
  The model drisspg/fp8-opt-125m was quantized with an older torchao that used
   float8 config version 1, but the torchao version in your torch 2.11 image
  expects version 2. This is a breaking change in torchao's
  _float8_dynamic_activation_float8_weight_quantize_tensor.

  The flow is:
  1. TorchAOConfig.from_config detects is_checkpoint_torchao_serialized = True
   (the model has quant_method: torchao)
  2. During create_weights, it calls torchao_quantize_param_data → quantize_()
   to pre-quantize weights
  3. torchao's quantize_() hits the version assertion because the model's
  config is v1

  This isn't something fixable in vllm — the model checkpoint itself is
  incompatible with the newer torchao. The options are:

  1. Re-quantize the model with the new torchao and push an updated
  drisspg/fp8-opt-125m
  2. Skip the test for this torch version (if this is a CI concern)
  3. Use a different fp8 test model that was quantized with the newer torchao


<details>

comments.body:
cc @jerryzh168 @drisspg I think these tests are failing because they use models that were created with version 1 quantization configs. Is the solution to regenerate the models?

`pytest "tests/quantization/test_torchao.py::test_pre_quantized_model"` uses `drisspg/fp8-opt-125m` and is failing with `Unexpected version: 1`

`pytest "tests/quantization/test_torchao.py::test_opt_125m_int4wo_model_per_module_quant"` uses `jerryzh168/opt-125m-int4wo-per-module` and is failing with `Int4WeightOnlyConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'layout'`
This issue is confirmed on latest runs: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/52665#019c8732-8ed9-4b91-ac61-db6e483db352

cc @atalman @angelayi Yeah I think we just need to regenerate these models, Jerry is out right now though, so we might have to change the model string in the text as well. Is that OK? 

I can regenerate the models now.

Actually I think we want to migrate `drisspg/fp8-opt-125m` to 
- https://huggingface.co/torchao-testing/opt-125m-Float8WeightOnlyConfig-v2-0.15.0

and delete the test for `jerryzh168/opt-125m-int4wo-per-module`, there already are test for the int4 v2 config
@jcaip Is this issue resolved now that the VLLM PR is merged?
Yes this should be resolved now. cc @atalman

I want to reopen this issue because I can see it manifested still when testing vLLM with PyTorch 2.11 RC https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch-integration-testing/actions/runs/22740523777/job/66007307931#step:19:8079.

* torchao nightly failed 
* torchao==0.16.0 failed
* ~~torchao==0.15.0 seem to work, but according to https://github.com/pytorch/ao/issues/2919, it's not compatible with 2.11.0.  I have been ignored the warning message~~ Nah, 0.15 seems to resolve the int4 problem, but fails on fp8 https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch-integration-testing/actions/runs/22819403513/job/66189714313#step:19:1979

As expected, newer torchao versions fails because quantized models like https://huggingface.co/pytorch/gemma-3-27b-it-INT4 haven't been updated with newer torchao versions

cc @jainapurva @jerryzh168
cc @huydhn I think we need to regenerate those models as well. I can do that, but I don't think I have access to the `pytorch` hf space - do you know who could give me access?

> cc [@huydhn](https://github.com/huydhn) I think we need to regenerate those models as well. I can do that, but I don't think I have access to the `pytorch` hf space - do you know who could give me access?

I think @jainapurva is on it.  I don't have access there too, only core team

An update on this that @jainapurva updated a new version of `pytorch/gemma-3-27b-it-INT4` yesterday, but the test still fails coming from transformers version.

```
It seems to be related to the transformers version vLLM is currently using 4.57.5 according to Claude
  Bug: When using pytorch/gemma-3-27b-it-INT4 (Gemma 3) with a transformers v4 version that doesn't have full_attention/sliding_attention
  in ALLOWED_LAYER_TYPES, the nested rope_parameters dict isn't recognized as nested. The code then tries to validate the outer dict
  directly (which has layer type keys, not rope_type), causing "rope_parameters should have a 'rope_type' key".
```

vLLM uses transformers 4.57.5 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/requirements/test.in#L40, so we need to use this same version, and update HF one more time.

After using transformers 4.57.5 and updating the models on HF, CI run on VLLM benchmarks has been successfully completed: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch-integration-testing/actions/runs/22963173889/job/66659289633
The issue seems to be resolved now.
Closing, this has been resolved. Confirmed by https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch-integration-testing/actions/runs/22972887664/job/66727676014
